variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept / precise spacecraft identity preservation.
Create ONE rear-completion design sheet for the user's SELECTED Freelancer Rheinland pirate fighter F14, "Draugr". This is the SAME selected spacecraft seen from behind, not a new ship or a redesign of its front. Invent only the previously unseen REAR skin of its transverse circular drum, recessed service fields and short engine attachment fairings, following the variant brief.

REFERENCE ROLES:
Image 1 is the selected F14, the authority for the entire silhouette, scale, volumes, wing shapes, forward hull, colors and existing FRONT drum surface. Its top and side define the proportions; its large perspective defines recess depths. Preserve its narrow long wedge body, sloping roof, recessed angular side fields, short forward-swept wings on recessed compact root sockets, two small longitudinal engine pods under the left/right lower edges of the drum, and slim tall circular drum. This image shows the FRONT face of the drum; DO NOT simply call that face a rear view.
Image 2 is the actual immutable RH fighter cockpit, including shell, blunt chin, blue pane layout, glazing frames, size and position. Reuse that exact cockpit wherever visible. No canopy change or enlargement. Its old surrounding body/drum are NOT a rear-design reference.

FIXED CONSTRUCTION:
The circular drum is a FIXED closed structural housing with its axis ALONG the ship. The circular faces look forward and aft, like a transverse upright disk. It is thin in side view. Keep EXACT selected diameter, thickness and overall volume; no enlargement, ball, wheel hub, propeller, fan, open cage or third engine. Preserve the front trapezoidal recessed vent field exactly as F14; the NEW rear surface is distinct.
Exactly TWO engines remain at the selected low-left and low-right positions (approximately 5 and 7 o'clock seen from behind), longitudinal axes parallel, same diameter/length/separation. Each has a complete short attached housing and a dark recessed exhaust bore. Engines do not emerge from the center of the drum. No flames obscuring geometry.
The original top cargo lid slides BACKWARD and slightly upward into a receiving pocket under the drum and BETWEEN the engines. Keep the existing closed top lid and reserve that center path inside the lower body. Show a modest recessed lower-center pocket mouth with real dark backing/inner walls, not a new giant through-hole, exhaust, pivoting hatch or solid engine-to-engine pedestal. Rear studies are in FLIGHT with cargo CLOSED. Do not invent an open cargo state or claim measured animation.
Wings preserve the original F14 forward sweep, short thick angled plates, clipped tips and compact recessed roots. No longer wings or new fins. Leave room around roots for their later inward/upward fold; no pipes, frames or supports across them.
Use coherent angular medium-size closed recesses and stepped skin surfaces inside the existing drum envelope. Avoid protruding decorative plates, exposed tubing, external framework, skulls, demonic motifs, military flags, Liberty Art Deco, new tail, spikes, random greebles and dense modeled rivets. Calm native pale metal with muted brick-red donor plates, dark brown recesses, limited yellow/black marks already on F14. Some service wear like F14, fully maintained intact ship. Small fasteners are texture only.

PRESENTATION:
One landscape sheet, pale neutral background, clear industrial concept rendering matching image 1.
LEFT TWO-THIRDS: large full-ship REAR 3/4, viewed from behind and above at an oblique angle. The NEW aft face of the drum and BOTH exhaust openings face the viewer. The long narrow body extends AWAY from the viewer beyond the drum, with cabin and wings visible to establish the unchanged whole spacecraft. Frame the ENTIRE ship with margins; no cropped tail close-up.
RIGHT TOP: true straight REAR elevation of the SAME variant, clear circular outline, both nozzles, wing relationships and lower-center recess. No false front view: canopy is on the far side and mainly hidden by the drum.
RIGHT BOTTOM: small FRONT 3/4 identity check, faithfully reproducing selected F14's existing front surface and original cockpit. It must not acquire the new rear treatment on its front face.
Keep all three drawings structurally consistent. All views show the same wing flight pose. Label only the variant ID, REAR 3/4, REAR, FRONT REFERENCE. Rear rendering is primary; no extra alternative ships or construction arrows.

REAR DESIGN R01: A calm stepped service shield. Inside the unchanged circular rear rim, use a large shallow angular six-sided inset plate, slightly taller than wide, with a narrow complete dark recessed perimeter. Divide it into THREE broad unequal service panels with readable horizontal/diagonal seams. A pale upper panel and muted red lower-left donor panel. Two small closed trapezoid recesses at the lower sides lead visually to the existing engine sockets. No central projecting boss; rear stays shallow and almost planar. Short solid engine collars integrated in the rim's lower sectors. The small lower-center cargo receiving pocket stays below the rear plate, between the pods. Title 'F14 / R01'.
